raw_response:
I will do it much like I did before, because on 13.1 mu I cannot play guessing games. If wheat or maize goes thin, that loss hurts more than wasting a bit of fertilizer. I farm by what I have seen work in our area. Around here, if wheat wants a steady stand, I give it a solid base fertilizer, water it a few times from the well, and do one topdressing when it starts pulling up strong. Maize is the same idea: get the seedlings up evenly, feed it before the big jointing stretch, and do not let it go thirsty at tasseling. I do not like fancy changes. If a hybrid seed did well in other people’s fields, I will use that kind. For wheat, I will keep fertilizer a bit heavier than a poor year, because land only gives grain if I feed it. For maize, I will also keep the fertilizer on the safe side. Pesticide, I will not spray blindly, but I will plan for about two times on each crop, because if disease or insects get ahead of me, catching up costs more. On this size of land, with just two people at home, rotary tillage is the handiest. It saves labor and I can finish on time.
